name: William Marks
role: Stake president at Kirtland and Nauvoo
dateNote: Section 117 called him to Far West on 8 July 1838; he became Nauvoo stake president on 5 October 1839.
importance: William Marks presided over the Church in Kirtland in 1838. Section 117 tells him to settle his business and preside at Far West, but the Missouri conflict stopped that plan. In 1839 he became stake president at Commerce, later Nauvoo, and section 124 asks him to buy Nauvoo House stock and ordain Isaac Galland. After Joseph Smith’s death he backed Sidney Rigdon and James Strang, and in 1859 joined the Reorganized Church.
connections: Section 117 pairs him with Bishop Newel K. Whitney, and section 124 links him with Isaac Galland and Hyrum Smith.

sources.title: William Marks, Joseph Smith Papers biography
